title: Request resource cleanup
summary: Recovered VA 0x4a1bc0 (RVA 0xa1bc0), 111 bytes, as readable C++ with i386 thiscall entry and stdcall interface callbacks. Calls virtual slot +8 for fields +0x440, +0x43c, +0x448, +0x444, conditionally on non-null, ignores callback results, and returns true in AL. Preserves the original load-next-before-clear-previous timing. Direct original disassembly and the request dispatcher case-1 caller at 0x4a1a61 were inspected. Accepted oracle bytes were checked against Game.exe and all 111 bytes agree. GCC freestanding differential executable passed.
test_description: 96 original-versus-recovered cases: all 16 pointer-presence masks, distinct versus aliased interface pointers, and three callback modes (no mutation, replacing all fields plus sentinel mutations, clearing all fields). Compares boolean result, callback order/count, complete owner and tail snapshots at each callback, per-interface call counts, and final byte image. Independent assertions check fixed callback order, clearing, untouched prefix/tail bytes, and repeated cleanup with no callbacks. Callback return values include zero and high-bit-set nonzero values. Oracle linked at VA 0x4a1bc0; test_main returns zero.
known_limits: Interface identities and resource ownership semantics are unresolved; slot +8 is Release-compatible, but no concrete COM interface is asserted.
The recovered layout names only the four known pointer fields. Unknown bytes and test tail are opaque; the enclosing object's complete type and size are not reconstructed.

Original callback calls leave ECX holding the interface pointer incidentally, while passing the interface through the stack with callee cleanup. The declared callback contract is stdcall; callbacks requiring a private extra register contract are not established by this evidence.
Null owner, invalid/dangling interface pointers, throwing callbacks, reentrant cleanup, and concurrent modification are not tested or assigned safe behavior.
Only AL is a defined return value in the original. Upper EAX bits and other caller-saved register residue are not part of the recovered boolean API.
Behavior validation uses instrumented interface callbacks rather than live game resources. This is high-level unmatched recovery, not a matching C++ rebuild.
